question: Can matt run it entirely from Vietnam with no physical hardware to buy, ship, place or touch anywhere?
How cheap is it per account per month at thousands to hundreds of thousands of accounts (infrastructure only, proxy excluded)?
How reliably does it keep accounts running day after day (uptime, sessions surviving restarts, few crashes or vendor outages)?
How easily does it grow from 10 to 100,000+ accounts without new cross-account linkage, quota walls or cost cliffs?
How easily can accounts be moved to another provider or service later (no lock-in, environment portable)?
How well does it serve platforms beyond Facebook Marketplace (other marketplaces, social sites, mobile-first apps)?
Can every account's traffic exit only through its own 2Captcha residential proxy, with the host's own datacenter IP never touching the platform?
Can matt watch and take over any account's live session (live desktop/VNC/stream) when needed?
Does each account get its own genuine canvas/WebGL rendering, not shared with our other accounts or the provider's other customers?
Does the device tell no contradictions (GPU name vs pixels, OS vs fonts, engine vs UA) and look like an ordinary home device rather than a VM, datacenter or emulator?
If one account is banned, how well are the others protected from being linked (device, cookies, IP, host, renderer)?
Can we run our leak and detection test suite (CreepJS-style checks, launch self-check, the 22 identityLeaks) inside the environment before an account goes live?
How well does it reuse log-cli (Camoufox gate, launch self-check, pinned device in Twenty, local hours, proxy handling)?
How little day-to-day work does it need at scale (maintenance, babysitting, updates)?
How strong is the independent evidence that it works against Meta-style detection, rather than vendor claims?
How well do we keep control of cookies, credentials and sessions (not held by a third party)?
